title: NextLayer._next_layer decision order (TLS/HTTP/QUIC/TCP/UDP/DNS)
answers: How does next_layer choose a protocol layer?
Where is the decision between TCPLayer, HttpLayer, TLS, QUIC made?
What order are rules evaluated in next_layer?
body:
All in `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py`. Hook `NextLayer.next_layer` skips if `nextlayer.layer` already set, else calls `_next_layer(ctx, data_client, data_server)`. `NeedsMoreData` from helpers defers the decision; hook refires with more bytes.
First match wins in `_next_layer`:
1. `_ignore_connection` true -> `TCPLayer(ignore=not show_ignored_hosts)` / `UDPLayer(...)`.
2. Fixed-mode: `_setup_reverse_proxy` (scheme -> LayerStack of Server/ClientTLS, Quic, HttpLayer, DNS...), `_setup_explicit_http_proxy` (HttpProxy/HttpUpstreamProxy; ClientQuic for UDP, ClientTLS if TLS-like, then HttpLayer regular/upstream).
3. `starts_like_tls_record` / `starts_like_dtls_record` -> ServerTLSLayer + ClientTLSLayer; UDP `_starts_like_quic` -> ServerQuicLayer + ClientQuicLayer.
4. `--tcp-hosts`/`--udp-hosts` via `_is_destination_in_hosts` (server.address[0] and client.sni). Runs after step 3, so SNI matches only on the second pass after TLS is set up.
5. ALPN in `HTTP_ALPNS` -> HttpLayer(transparent); other ALPN with QUICv1 -> `RawQuicLayer(force_raw=True)`; port 53/5353 -> DNSLayer; other UDP -> UDPLayer; TCP: rawtcp && `probably_no_http` -> TCPLayer else HttpLayer(transparent).
`NextLayer.configure` compiles tcp_hosts/udp_hosts/ignore_hosts/allow_hosts to case-insensitive regexes.
